messages:
auditor_jb: Hi team — for SOC 2 and ISO evidence we need: proof that customer CMKs are on automatic rotation (or equivalent policy), RBAC changes are captured in audit logs (who changed what and when), and emergency/just-in-time admin access events are recorded. Can you provide the specific log queries and sample results?

alex: Thanks. We'll gather a minimal artifact set: key rotation status, KMS key policy snippet, CloudTrail query + sample events for AssumeRole, and the RBAC change deployment record (git commit + deploy job).

mira: Putting links together. Evidence artifacts will be in s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/soc2/2026-03-kms-rbac/ — contains: kms-rotation-status.txt, kms-policy.json, cloudtrail-assumerole-sample.log, rbac-deploy-commit.txt, incident-emt-access.log.

kevin: For RBAC changes we use git + deploy pipeline. Minimal query to match auditor ask: `git log --pretty=format:\"%h %an %ad %s\" --since=2026-02-01 --grep=rbac` and our deploy bot posts job run ids to #eng-releases. Sample entry in rbac-deploy-commit.txt: `commit 9f4b2e1 by alex 2026-03-10: update role bindings -> ROLE:service-admin -> added infra-team`

mira: KMS rotation check (I ran this):
```
$ aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id alias/rdw-customer-master
{"KeyId": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789","KeyRotationEnabled": true}
```
Attached file: kms-rotation-status.txt (same output)

kevin: KMS policy excerpt (kms-policy.json):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid":"EnableRotation","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-kms-admin"},"Action":["kms:EnableKeyRotation","kms:DisableKeyRotation"],"Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:PrincipalTag/team":"security"}}}
  ]
}
```

auditor_jb: OK — rotation true is good. For emergency access I need a timestamped AssumeRole event showing who assumed the role, source IP, and the STS session duration. Can you include a raw CloudTrail entry (redact IP if necessary) and the timestamp that matches your incident ticket?

kevin: Copying cloudtrail query we used: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRole --start-time 2026-03-09T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-12T23:59:59Z` Sample (cloudtrail-assumerole-sample.log):
```
{\n  "EventId": "e3a1b2c4-...",\n  "EventTime": "2026-03-11T19:42:33Z",\n  "Username": "alex@example.com",\n  "EventName": "AssumeRole",\n  "Resources": [{"ARN":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/emergency-admin"}],\n  "SourceIPAddress": "REDACTED",\n  "AdditionalEventData": {"SessionDuration": 3600}\n}
```
Linked file: incident-emt-access.log (contains raw CloudTrail JSON with sensitive fields redacted).

mira: Also included the incident ticket reference: SEC-2026-77. In the ticket we documented approval workflow (chat logs + JIT approval form) and attached the post-incident review. Evidence path: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/soc2/2026-03-kms-rbac/SEC-2026-77/***

auditor_jb: Good. One more: please map the artifacts to controls — e.g., which file shows evidence for SOC2 CC6 (change management) vs SOC2 CC7 (access control). A simple mapping doc is fine.

alex: Will add control-mapping.csv in the same folder. Quick mapping preview: `kms-rotation-status.txt -> CC6.5/KeyMgmt; cloudtrail-assumerole-sample.log -> CC7.1/JIT access; rbac-deploy-commit.txt -> CC6.3/ChangeRecords; rbac-deploy-job.log -> CC6.4/ChangeApproval`

kevin: Also noting we found a small vuln during this window (dependency lib-auth v2.3.1 CVE-2025-12345). Triage: created VULN-412, applied patch to staging 2026-03-08, scheduled production rollback/patch on 2026-03-12. Evidence in s3 path above under vuln-triage/ (report + patch PR link).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: RBAC update pipeline completed: job 4827, commit 9f4b2e1, status: SUCCESS, timestamp: 2026-03-10T21:05:12Z :white_check_mark:

security-bot: compliance-helper: evidence bundle uploaded to s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/soc2/2026-03-kms-rbac/ (kms-rotation-status.txt, cloudtrail-assumerole-sample.log, rbac-deploy-commit.txt, control-mapping.csv, SEC-2026-77-postmortem.pdf)

auditor_jb: Thanks — I'll review the bundle tonight and follow up if I need raw logs unredacted under a secure transfer. Appreciate the mapping preview, that speeds review. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks all. If auditor needs a signed attest or export to their portal we can schedule a secure transfer window.

mira: I'll add a one-page readme in the folder describing each file and the exact command we ran to extract the logs (so auditors can replicate).

auditor_jb: Perfect. Closing the request for now, will reopen if anything else is required.
